title: Distributed Edge-Fog Architecture for Path Tracking in Geo-Referenced Mobile Robots via Low-Cost LPWAN Networks
content: The convergence of mobile robotics with telecommunications has driven the emergence of the Internet of Robotic Things (IoRT). However, deploying autonomous robots in unstructured environments faces a critical limitation: the unpredictable latency and high costs of the traditional Cloud Robotics model make it unfeasible in rural, agricultural, or remote industrial contexts with only low-speed network access. This paper presents a distributed Edge-Fog architecture for geo-referenced path tracking over low-cost LPWAN networks. The Fog layer, orchestrated with Node-RED, handles route planning and spatially compresses trajectories (String Pulling) to make transmission over the limited LoRa spectrum feasible. The Edge layer, based on an STM32 microcontroller running FreeRTOS, autonomously manages inertial sensor fusion (GPS and IMU), heading tracking through a proportional-derivative (PD) controller with Cross-Track Error (XTE) correction, and reactive obstacle avoidance via a Fuzzy Inference System (FIS). Link reliability is guaranteed through a Stop-and-Wait ARQ flow-control protocol with automatic retries and duplicate tolerance. The experimental results validate the proposal: a Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) of 100%, a 93%-96% reduction in navigation data transmitted over LoRa, and successful reactive avoidance of both static and dynamic obstacles, confirming the feasibility of democratizing advanced mobile robotics without saturating low-bandwidth channels.
